before_notes: Pure BM1370 protocol core now covers framing/CRC, the init plan split at chip detection, the BM1370 PLL range, the bidirectional ramp, the errata nonce space, 82-byte work and 88-byte job frames, 24-step job ids, strict result/register/chip-id decoding, and pinned-reference golden fixtures; see docs/parity/evidence/asic008-bm1370-core/summary.md and docs/parity/work-plans/20261023T180521Z-ASIC-008/WORKLOG.md. Firmware dispatch, UART/device effects, chip counting, and Gamma 601 hardware verification remain unavailable and unclaimed.
after_notes: The pure BM1370 core (docs/parity/evidence/asic008-bm1370-core/summary.md) drives the Gamma 601 firmware through its 601 ASIC and mining adapters. On the 601's one BM1370, a bounded check counted one chip, and a known-job hash check returned 8 verified nonces and no invalid ones at 300 MHz. Local mining accepted shares with none rejected at 400 MHz and at upstream's 525 MHz / 1150 mV default, for 10 minutes each, and for 4 hours of mining (440 shares, mean 1068 GH/s, one Wi-Fi outage recovered) on test builds. The promoted production build then resumed mining on boot, passed the self-test at 1028.4 GH/s across four domains, and ran a 10-minute smoke soak (39 shares, mean 1063 GH/s). See docs/parity/work-plans/20261029T040601Z-ASIC-008/RESULT.md. Live frequency changes, mining from a power-on boot, multi-hour runs of the production build, the thermal margin in a warmer room (the 75 C trip ended one production run at this profile), other BM1370 boards and chip counts, and release readiness remain non-claims.
